title: A Moon City for a Million People? Scientists Say the Water Would Run Out
summary:
Could a million people live on the Moon? Two scientists ran the numbers, and their answer is: yes, but not for very long. The problem is not power. The problem is water.

SpaceX chief Elon Musk has said his company is now focused on building a self-growing city on the Moon in less than 10 years, while a Mars city would take more than 20 years. Blue Origin chief Jeff Bezos has said millions of people will be living in space by 2045. Those claims caught the attention of Martin Elvis, an astrophysicist at Harvard University's Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, and Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist at Durham University in England.

In a paper in the journal Frontiers in Space Technologies, the pair looked at what a Moon settlement would need. For power, they found that solar and nuclear energy could support one million people on the lunar surface.

Water is trickier. There is water on the Moon, mostly hidden in permanently shadowed regions near the poles. But the scientists found there is not enough of it for a huge population.

Assuming the Moon holds about one billion tonnes of water, a city of one million people could last only about 100 years, and only if 98 percent of the water is recycled, the same rate as on the International Space Station. Elvis compared that water to a giant aquarium the size of Central Park in New York, filled until the Statue of Liberty would be just underwater. Huge, he said, but still only a small lake.

A smaller settlement would fare better. A town of 10,000 people, the study found, could last for centuries. But Elvis said the one-billion-tonne estimate is probably far too high, perhaps 20 or 30 times too big. So do not start packing just yet.
why_it_matters: Big plans for living in space sound exciting, but this study shows that a basic need like water can set the real limit, and checking the numbers matters before promises are believed.

background_read: A settlement is a place where people live, work and build a community far from home.
On the Moon there is no air to breathe and no ready supply of water, so a settlement would have to find, carry or reuse everything its people need.
Solar power uses sunlight to make energy, and nuclear power makes energy from atoms, so both can work on the Moon without fuel shipped from Earth.
Recycling water means cleaning and using the same water again and again, which matters most when there is no new water to replace it.
Article_Structure: LEAD: Two scientists say a million-person Moon city could work, but not for very long, because water would run out.
KEY EVENT: Martin Elvis and Jonathan McDowell checked what a Moon settlement would need, in a paper in Frontiers in Space Technologies.
├─ WHO: Elon Musk, who wants a self-growing Moon city in less than 10 years, and Jeff Bezos, who says millions of people will live in space by 2045.
├─ WHAT: Solar and nuclear energy could support one million people, but there is not enough water for a huge population.
└─ WHEN: A city of one million could last only about 100 years if 98 percent of its water is recycled.
EVIDENCE: Elvis compared the water to a giant aquarium the size of Central Park, filled until the Statue of Liberty would be just underwater, yet still only a small lake.
OPEN QUESTION: Elvis said the one-billion-tonne estimate is probably far too high, so a big Moon city may be even harder than the numbers suggest.
